question: Do the already-frozen white-paint axes recur across unrelated standardized glyph systems strongly enough to justify a physical-witness historical test?

corpus.status: standardized display proxies, not physical archaeological or manuscript witnesses

frozenOperators.loop_continue: enclosed void present and at least one skeleton terminal remains
frozenOperators.close: enclosed void present and no skeleton terminal remains
frozenOperators.cross: single component, no enclosed void, and a junction cluster reaches local degree >= 4
frozenOperators.branch: single component, no enclosed void, at least one junction cluster, and at least three terminals
frozenOperators.turn: single component, no enclosed void, no junction cluster, exactly two terminals, local degree-2 turn rate >= 0.08
frozenOperators.persist: single component, no enclosed void, no junction cluster, exactly two terminals, local degree-2 turn rate < 0.08

frozenRelation.eligible: at least one clustered junction and at least one skeleton terminal
frozenRelation.nearTerminal: minimum junction-to-terminal Euclidean distance divided by glyph diagonal <= 0.22

frozenDegree.proxy: clip degree-3 junction-cluster count to integer range 0..5
frozenDegree.theoryOriginPositiveControl: Within the first four visible Ogham 5-sign runs, ordinal position 1..5 should correlate with endpoints + junctionClusters + degree3JunctionClusters. This is a positive control motivated before v2 and is not independent universality evidence.

frozenClosure.closed: one or more enclosed raster voids
frozenClosure.note: This display-proxy lane intentionally uses literal raster voids, avoiding the v1 critical-center cycle-rank blind spot for degree-2-only loops.

predictions.prediction: At least five of persist/turn/branch/cross/close/loop_continue occur in four or more independent script systems, and no passing operation is supplied more than 60% by a single system.
Near-terminal and interior attachment both occur in at least five script systems, and relation-feature nearest-neighbor cross-system mixing exceeds modifier-shape-only mixing by at least 0.05.
At least four script systems contain three or more distinct positive repetition-degree proxy values; at least three of the four predeclared Ogham positive-control runs achieve Spearman rho >= 0.80.
Both open and closed forms occur in at least seven independent script systems, with no single system supplying more than 50% of closed forms.

Three-nearest-neighbor system-identity accuracy from white-paint structural features is at least 0.05 lower than accuracy from appearance features, indicating greater cross-system mixing in the proposed substrate than in rendered style.

nullModel.method: shuffle post-freeze system labels across the frozen blind records while preserving the exact system-size multiset; never alter physical features or blind classes
nullModel.purpose: measure whether observed cross-system recurrence/mixing differs from arbitrary reassignment of the same glyph structures

claimBoundary.allowed: The frozen white-paint structural axes do or do not recur across a standardized cross-system glyph proxy corpus under predeclared transfer tests.
forbidden: Atlas meaning assigned to an ancient sign

nextGateIfSupported: Harvest governed physical witnesses for multiple script traditions, freeze witness lanes before extraction, and repeat the same operator/relation/degree/closure transfer without standardized Unicode forms.
